question.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by 

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{n}.
$$

Find ${a}_{n},$ given that

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}.
$$
question.worked_solution:
Writing the terms of the series explicitly, we have

$$
f(x)={x}^{3}+\frac{{x}^{5}}{2}+⋯+{{\frac{{x}^{2n+1}}{n}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

Differentiating the above series term-by-term gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & =3{x}^{2}+\frac{5{x}^{4}}{2}+⋯+{{\frac{(2n+1){x}^{2n}}{n}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write the Taylor series for ${f}^{′}(x)$ using the sigma notation as follows:

$$
{f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(2n+1){x}^{2n}}{n}
$$

Comparing the series above with the given series, we can deduce that

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{(2n+1){x}^{2n}}{n}.
$$
